chunks: From him, from ʿAlī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about madhy that comes onto the garment and clings to it. He said: “He washes it, and he does not perform wudu (ablution).”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, the author of this book, said: These two reports are to be understood as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation, as shown by the reports we have mentioned earlier. What further clarifies that is what this very narrator himself has narrated, and it is:

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing onto which the substance falls
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the narrations or reports used as evidence
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here as a source affecting ritual purity rulings
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu (ablution), which is negated here
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهُ: he washes it, meaning the affected part of the garment

ai.seo_question: Does madhy on clothing require washing and invalidate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of madhy when it soils a garment, stating that the affected area should be washed but that wudu (ablution) is not required. The compiler then explains that some related reports are understood in the sense of recommendation rather than obligation, showing a juristic method of reconciling narrations.
